raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

- refresh AITER unified attention's stable CUDA Graph page-table buffer when `page_size == 1`
- preserve the existing page-index transformation for larger page sizes
- add HIP regression coverage for both token-level and paged layouts

Without this copy, non-SWA unified-attention decode replays can consume zero or stale KV indices at page size 1. This affects ROCm Mamba radix-cache configurations that use `no_buffer` while keeping CUDA Graph enabled.

## Test plan

- [x] Run `test_aiter_fp8_q_unified_attention.py` on ROCm/MI308X: 4 tests passed
- [x] Run TP4 Qwen3.5-397B GSM8K with AITER unified attention, CUDA Graph, and `no_buffer` radix cache enabled
- [x] Verify 300-sample GSM8K strict accuracy: baseline 0.9767, DFLASH 0.9667
- [x] Verify repeated 200-sample runs do not show cumulative accuracy degradation or invalid page-table reads

Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

nodes.body:
Gentle ping — this PR is stuck before CI rather than in review.

All `pr-gate` jobs fail within a few seconds with:

```
Missing required label 'run-ci'. See https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests
```

so every downstream test job is skipped and no CI has actually run yet. I don't have triage permission on this repo, so I can't add the label myself.

@HaiShaw @hebiao064 — could one of you add `run-ci`? This is a ROCm-only change (+67/-2, 2 files): it refreshes AITER unified attention's stable CUDA Graph page-table buffer when `page_size == 1`, and leaves the page-index transformation for larger page sizes untouched. Without it, non-SWA unified-attention decode replays can consume zero or stale KV indices at page size 1, which breaks ROCm Mamba radix-cache setups running `no_buffer` with CUDA Graph enabled. A regression test covering both the token-level and paged layouts is included.

Thanks!
+1 from our side: we hit the same bug and opened #41234 before finding this PR. Gemma 2/3 are affected too, since unified attention is their only aiter decode path. Closing mine in favor of this one.

Hi @bingxche @kkHuang-amd @HaiShaw @hebiao064 — could one of you add the `run-ci` label (or comment `/tag-and-rerun-ci`) on this PR?

CI is still blocked at `pr-gate` (`Require run-ci label`), so no tests have actually run yet. I'm not in `CI_PERMISSIONS.json` and don't have triage permission, so I can't trigger it myself.

This is a small ROCm-only fix (+67/-2, 2 files) for stale/zero KV indices in AITER unified attention CUDA Graph replay at `page_size == 1`. #41234 was closed as a duplicate of this one, and Gemma 2/3 are affected as well. Thanks!

Scope is required and may be any module or model name, with unrestricted letter case (letters, numbers, dots, underscores, slashes, or hyphens). Hardware is optional; use a single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend. Reverts must use GitHub's default format: Revert "original title". Use one space between fields and after the colon, with a non-empty title and no leading or trailing whitespace. Examples: "[Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing", "[Feat] qwen3: Add model support", "[Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance".
Edit the title; the check reruns on its own.

Hi @kkHuang-amd, thanks for the approval! I went through the CI failures on the latest run, and they are unrelated to this PR. The PR's own test (`test_aiter_fp8_q_unified_attention.py`) passed.

**PR Test (AMD)** ([run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39357351088)): all 4 failures reproduce identically on `main` scheduled runs (e.g. [39421857090](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39421857090), [39522599360](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39522599360)):
- `test_dsv4_hip_bcg_metadata.py`: `AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'swa_req_ring_size'` (stale mock vs. `deepseek_v4_backend.py`)
- `test_dsv41_bcg_hip.py`: `AssertionError: 2 != 1`
- `test_disaggregation_basic.py`: `CUDA error: out of memory` at scheduler startup, before any CUDA graph capture
- `test_kimi_k2_instruct.py`: hung in safetensors weight loading until the 1h timeout (MLA model, never reaches the changed branch)

**PR Test Extra** ([run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39357350969)): the only root-cause failure is `kv_canary/test_self_e2e_perturb_raise.py` (exit 137) on an RTX 5090 runner, which doesn't use the aiter backend. The same failure also hit the unrelated `ria/grpc-shutdown` branch twice the same day. The other jobs failed only because of the fail-fast cascade.

**PR Test (Base)** ([run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39357350976)): no test failures. Every completed job passed. 4 `base-b` jobs sat queued for about 2h44m without getting a runner, and then the run was cancelled.

This PR only touches the non-SWA, `spec_info is None` unified-attention decode CUDA graph replay path in `aiter_backend.py` (+9/-2), plus a unit test. Could you help re-run the failed jobs or merge if these are known issues? Thanks!

Hi @HaiShaw @hebiao064 — could one of you take a look and approve? This PR touches `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/aiter_backend.py`, so it needs a code-owner approval. @kkHuang-amd has already approved, but he isn't a code owner for `layers/attention`, so the PR is still blocked on review.

I rebased onto the latest main (`c43abd6`). The remaining CI failures are unrelated to this change:

- **`test_openai_server.py`** (PR Test (AMD), stage-b shard 2): the AMD image fails with `cannot import name 'ResponseFunctionShellToolCall' from 'openai.types.responses'`, so `openai_serving_responses` is never initialized and the test gets `500 != 400`. An unrelated PR hits the same failure on the same shard today ([job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40442233086/job/121989249312)).
- **`test_torch_compile_moe.py`, `test_torch_compile_throughput.py`, `test_score_api.py`**: these fail on perf thresholds (for example, 190 vs >= 240 tok/s), not on correctness.
- **`test_load_weights_from_remote_instance.py`**: the server connection is refused during remote weight loading.

The change itself only runs when `use_triton_unified_attention` is true, which means an SWA KV pool or `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1`. None of the failing tests enable either, so none of them reach the modified branch. The diff is +9/-2 in `aiter_backend.py` plus a unit test, and `test_aiter_fp8_q_unified_attention.py` passed on the previous CI run (it runs on the MI35x shard, which is still queued for this run).

Thanks!

+    def test_cuda_graph_page_table_is_refreshed_for_all_page_sizes(self):
+        req_to_token = torch.tensor(
+            [
+                [0, 1, 4, 5, 8, 9, 12, 13],
+                [20, 21, 24, 25, 28, 29, 32, 33],
+            ],
+            dtype=torch.int32,
+            device="cuda",
+        )
+        req_pool_indices = torch.tensor([1, 0], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+        seq_lens = torch.tensor([4, 3], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+        max_kv_len = int(seq_lens.max().item())
+
+        for page_size in (1, 2):
+            with self.subTest(page_size=page_size):
+                backend = object.__new__(AiterAttnBackend)
+                backend.use_mla = False
+                backend.use_triton_unified_attention = True
+                backend.use_sliding_window_kv_pool = False
+                backend.max_context_len = req_to_token.shape[1]
+                backend.page_size = page_size
+                backend.req_to_token = req_to_token
+                backend.cuda_graph_page_table = torch.full(
+                    (
+                        len(req_pool_indices),
+                        req_to_token.shape[1] // page_size,
+                    ),
+                    -1,
+                    dtype=torch.int32,
+                    device="cuda",
+                )
+                backend.qo_indptr_unified_decode = torch.arange(
+                    len(req_pool_indices) + 1,
+                    dtype=torch.int32,
+                    device="cuda",
+                )
+
+                backend._apply_cuda_graph_metadata(
+                    bs=len(req_pool_indices),
+                    req_pool_indices=req_pool_indices,
+                    seq_lens=seq_lens,
+                    seq_lens_sum=int(seq_lens.sum().item()),
+                    forward_mode=ForwardMode.DECODE,
+                    spec_info=None,
+                    seq_lens_cpu=seq_lens.cpu(),
+                    verify_tokens_per_req=None,
+                )
+
+                expected = req_to_token[req_pool_indices, :max_kv_len]
+                if page_size > 1:
+                    expected = expected[:, ::page_size] // page_size
+                actual = backend.forward_metadata.kv_indices[
+                    : len(req_pool_indices), : expected.shape[1]
+                ]
+                torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected)
